en: The Sūtra on a Bhikṣu Attempting Suicide to Avoid the Evil Reputation of a Woman, translated by the Western Jin śramaṇa Dharmakṣema.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, there was a certain bhikṣu living in a forest in the human realm of Kosala.
At that time, that bhikṣu dallied with the wives of householders, giving rise to an evil reputation.
Then that bhikṣu thought to himself:
"I must not now incur an evil reputation by being with another's wife; I wish instead to take my own life here in this forest!"
At that time, a deva dwelling in that grove thought to himself:
"This is wicked and unwholesome; it is not fitting for this.
This bhikṣu is undegenerated and faultless, yet he wishes to take his own life in the forest. I shall now go there and awaken him through skillful means!"
Then that deva transformed himself into the body of a householder’s daughter and said to the bhikṣu:

“In the various streets and at the crossroads, people of the world have brought an evil reputation upon both me and you, saying that we have become intimate and are committing improper acts together.”
“Since we already have an ill reputation, you may now return to secular life so that we may enjoy ourselves together.

The bhikṣu replied, “Because of our association with you in the lanes and crossroads of that village, an evil report has arisen concerning me; since we have engaged in improper conduct together, I shall now take my own life.”
Then that deva returned to his celestial form and spoke this verse:
"Though one hears many evil reports, the ascetic endures them;
He should not harm himself through suffering, nor should he give rise to vexation."
Those who feel terror at the sound of voices are like wild beasts in the forest;
such fickle beings do not fulfill the way of renunciation.
O virtuous one, you must endure low, middling, and high-voiced abuse.
One whose mind is firmly established is practicing the way of the renunciant.
It is not by another’s words that you are made a thief, nor is it by another that you attain arhatship.
"As you yourself now know, so too do all the devas.
At that time, having been enlightened by that heavenly deity, the bhikṣu applied himself with focused diligence; he severed his afflictions and attained arhatship.
The Sūtra on the Bhikṣu Who Attempted Suicide to Avoid the Evil Reputation of a Woman.
